events.title: Nguyen Huu Canh established Gia Dinh Prefecture
events.description: Commander Nguyen Huu Canh, by order of Lord Nguyen Phuc Chu, went to inspect and govern the Southern region, officially establishing the administrative unit of Gia Dinh Prefecture (including Phuoc Long District and Tan Binh District). This event marked the birth of today's Saigon - Ho Chi Minh City on the administrative map of Dai Viet.

events.title: French attack on Gia Dinh Citadel
events.description: The French-Spanish coalition forces opened fire, attacked, and captured Gia Dinh Citadel. Although the royal army was defeated, local militia continuously harassed and ambushed them, forcing the French to use explosives to destroy this citadel in March 1859.

events.title: Uncle Ho leaves to find a way for national salvation
events.description: At Nha Rong Harbor, the young man Nguyen Tat Thanh (under the name Van Ba) boarded the ship Amiral Latouche Treville, beginning a 30-year journey across the oceans to find a path to liberate the Vietnamese nation.

events.title: The Ba Son strike
events.description: Under the leadership of the Red Union (organized by Ton Duc Thang), workers at the Ba Son Shipyard went on strike to prevent the French from repairing warships to suppress the Chinese revolution. This was the first political strike by the Vietnamese working class.

events.title: Cochinchina Uprising
events.description: The Cochinchina Party Committee issued the order for the uprising. In Saigon and surrounding areas (Hoc Mon, Go Vap...), the people rose up to attack outposts and cut telephone lines. Although it failed, this event marked the first appearance of the red flag with a yellow star and left a bloody lesson about armed uprising.
tags: Red flag with a yellow star

events.title: Seizing power in Saigon
events.description: More than 1 million compatriots in Saigon - Cho Lon - Gia Dinh took to the streets to demonstrate, seizing the Imperial Envoy's Palace, the Police Department, and key headquarters. The Provisional Administrative Committee of the Southern Region (Southern Provisional Committee) made its public debut, with Mr. Tran Van Giau as Chairman.

events.title: Southern Resistance Day
events.description: The French colonialists, supported by British troops, opened fire and captured the headquarters of the Southern People's Committee. The people of Saigon immediately erected barricades and destroyed roads, initiating the resistance war against the French re-invasion with the spirit of 'Rather die in freedom than live in slavery'.

events.title: Venerable Thich Quang Duc's self-immolation
events.description: At the intersection of Phan Dinh Phung and Le Van Duyet (now CMT8 - Nguyen Dinh Chieu), Venerable Thich Quang Duc self-immolated to protest the Buddhist persecution policies of the Ngo Dinh Diem administration. The image of the 'sacred fire' shocked the world, leading to the collapse of the Diem regime.

events.title: General Offensive and Uprising of Tet Mau Than (Saigon)
events.description: The Saigon Commandos and spearhead battalions launched sudden, simultaneous attacks on key targets: the US Embassy, Independence Palace, the Radio Station, the General Staff Headquarters... The battle shocked the United States, forcing the US to de-escalate the war and sit at the Paris peace talks.

events.title: Liberation of Saigon - National Reunification
events.description: At 11:30 AM, tanks 390 and 843 crashed through the gates of Independence Palace. President Duong Van Minh declared unconditional surrender. The flag of the National Liberation Front flew on the roof of the palace, the Ho Chi Minh Campaign achieved complete victory, ending 30 years of war and reunifying the country.

events.title: Officially named Ho Chi Minh City
events.description: At its first session, the 6th National Assembly (the unified National Assembly) issued a Resolution officially renaming Saigon - Gia Dinh City to Ho Chi Minh City. This was a great honor, affirming the position of the city named after Uncle Ho.
